Ciao, I'm Caroline. 
An object and spatial designer.
My experience spans different scales, from executing corporate and residential renovations to developing custom furniture and product solutions.

Born and raised in the Caribbean, I’ve been shaped by the eclectic and layered nature of my environments. As a multidisciplinary designer, my experience spans different scales, from executing corporate and residential renovations to developing furniture and product solutions. 
I find purpose in the evolution of a project, from research and concept, to the collaborative development of a well-crafted reality. Whether it is a furniture piece or a full-scale interior, I like design that demands attention, not by being bold or loud, but by inspiring stillness.
Master in Product and Furniture Design

Bachelor in Industrial Design
Instituto Tecnológico de Santo Domingo
2015–2019

This portfolio brings together selected projects that explore the same ideas in different formats. Each case looks at how structure, composition, texture, and space can support content without competing with it.
I’m open to freelance projects, collaborations, and selected full-time opportunities.
My work focuses on visual systems across furniture, and spatial contexts. If you’d like to discuss a project or ask a question,  feel free to reach out.

Based on the reimagination of the future of the domestic environment through product design and innovative technologies, the Domestic Oracle emerged. Looking into the past to reshape the future, I worked with time as a key factor in today’s source of stress, leading to toxic productivity.

The clock shows real time in a diffused, implicit manner through color gradients reflecting the sky’s natural course. Upon proximity with the user, changes colors in reaction to the user’s feelings and expressions, thus creating a non-verbal introspective moment amidst busy lifestyles.
Materiality and function merge to encompass the concept of embracing presence.

Adagio is an outdoor seating collection conceived for Cappellini, developed under the art direction of Piero Lissoni. It borrows its tempo from music — slow, deliberate, expansive. Tubular aluminium frames trace uninterrupted arcs. Perforated sheet panels hold light without weight. Polypropylene textiles anchor each element in warmth. Together, the armchair, sofa, and chaise longue compose a space where the invitation is simple: stay longer.
The collection is built on a 22mm tubular aluminium frame, powder-coated in a unifying terracotta. Backrest panels are formed in perforated aluminium sheet.
Seats and cushions are upholstered in polypropylene textile, for high performance and low maintenance.
Adagio takes its name and spirit from the musical direction:

A tempo that asks for slowness and full presence. Applied to outdoor furniture, this becomes a structural principle: forms that do not hurry, lines that extend beyond the strictly necessary, silhouettes that carry the eye outward before returning it to rest.
The project draws inspiration from the formal language of Roman mosaics, focusing on the compositional principles that define their enduring visual power.
Central to this is the idea of fragmentation, where individual tesserae form a cohesive whole, establishing a rhythm through repetition, variation, and subtle imperfection.
Like in ancient mosaics, each piece is both autonomous and essential. Removed from its context, it is incomplete; assembled, it becomes coherent.
Pieces emerge, break, and reconfigure, echoing the logic of fragmentation while embracing the imperfections of time.

mag.description: Ciao, I'm Caroline. An object and spatial designer. I'm interested in how products and spaces can create memorable experiences without being loud about it.
